text: When Leo arrived at the market, he noticed the various colors of fruits and vegetables in the stalls.
At a small stall, fruits were neatly arranged according to their color.

speaker: Vendor
text: Leo! Do you know how to sign colors yet?

speaker: Vendor
text: Good! Look at the fruit in the middle. What color is this?

speaker: Vendor
text: Correct! The tomato is red. That's a good example of the color RED.

speaker: Vendor
text: No. The apple is RED. Try looking at it again.

speaker: Vendor
text: No. The apple is RED. Try looking at it again.

speaker: Vendor
text: Now then, take a look at the leaf. What color is this?

speaker: Vendor
text: Correct! GREEN is the color of the leaf.

speaker: Vendor
text: No. The leaf is GREEN. Look closely at its color.

speaker: Vendor
text: No. The leaf is GREEN. Look closely at its color.

speaker: Vendor
text: Great job! Last one. Look at the banana. What color is this?

speaker: Vendor
text: Correct! YELLOW is the color of the banana.

speaker: Vendor
text: No. YELLOW is the color of the banana. Try again.

speaker: Vendor
text: No. YELLOW is the color of the banana. Try again.
Leo noticed that it was easier to recognize colors when he associated them with objects he saw around him.

speaker: Vendor
text: Before you go, would you like me to repeat any color signs, or are you ready to say goodbye?
Leaving the market, Leo tried observing things around him and naming their colors using the signs he had learned.

speaker: Vendor
text: Of course! Remember RED, GREEN, and YELLOW from the fruit and vegetables.

speaker: Vendor
text: Goodbye, Leo! Keep practicing the colors you saw today.
